text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Swedish astronomer ANDERS CELSIUS, who invented the Celsius temperature scale, was born in 1701.
Pioneer pastoralist CYRUS DOYLE was born in 1793. His original leasehold was the New South Wales town of Narrabri.
Scottish/Australian businessman and politician JAMES SERVICE was born in 1823. He was a major force in Federation.
The Australian comic strip character GINGER MEGGS was born in 1921. He first appeared in "Us Fellers" in the Sydney Sun.

United States guitarist, singer and songwriter JIMI HENDRIX, who taught himself to play guitar as a teenager, was born in 1942. In 1966 CHAS CHANDLER of the 'Animals' discovered him and took him to London and put together the trio 'Jimi Hendrix Experience'. Hits included "Purple Haze" (1967), "The Wind Cries Mary" (1967), "All Along the Watchtower" (1968) and "Voodoo Chile" (1970). HeNDRIX was one of the highlights of the Woodstock Festival with his own group 'Electric Sky Church'. JIMI died on 18th September 1970.

American singer/songwriter EDDIE RABBITT (EDWARD THOMAS), whose first records were unsuccessful, was born in 1944. EDDIE's first break came when ELVIS PRESLEY had a million seller with his song "Kentucky Rain". His own singles included "I Love A Rainy Night"(1980) "Step By Step" (1981) and with CRYSTAL GAYLE "You and I" in 1982.
** EVENTS **
1893 : For the first time anywhere in the world women

voted in a general election. It was the New Zealand national election. The female suffrage bill had been passed by the parliament by two votes and was largely due to the efforts of Liberal leader RICHARD JOHN SEDDON, known as "King DICK". SEDDON and the Liberals were returned to power.
1919 : A massive meteor landed in Lake Michigan.
1942 : Australian and American servicemen clashed in a
brawl which became known as the "Battle of Brisbane". One Australian was shot dead.
1963 : The Victorian Government set up an inquiry into
the Hubbard Association of Scientology. MPS accused the group of being charlatans and blackmailers.
1970 : The Gay Liberation Front held its first
demonstration in London.
1970 : In Manila, the capital of the Phillippines, a
knife-wielding man was seized as he attempted to attack Pope JOHN PAUL.
1977 : The first World Series Cricket match between
Australia and a World XI attracted only 10,043 people over four days to the Melbourne cricket grounds.
1988 : Queensland's former Transport Minister DON LANE

wept while giving evidence to the Fitzgerald Inquiry into corruption. The former minister was asked by TONY FITZGERALD QC to name former cabinet colleagues who had used public money for entertainment expenses.
1991 : A 15th-century Bible sold at Christie's in London
to a New York antiquarian bookseller for two million dollars.
